notes: Not on CCEL; the text is archive.org OCR of Vol. III of the 1857-58 T&T Clark edition (gnomonofthenewte00benguoft; title page MDCCCLVII, 'translated by Rev. James Bryce, M.A.'; the series title page reads 'revised and edited by Rev. Andrew R. Fausset', and the volume's own title page names Ernest Bengel and J. C. F. Steudel as editors of the Latin edition). Bengel's notes on the whole of Romans 1-16 are taken, cut by a script from the OCR: verses from his printed verse numbers under the CHAPTER heads; each Greek lemma is followed by its English or Latin gloss and a closing parenthesis, then the note. The OCR turns the Greek lemmas and the Greek or Hebrew inside the notes into garbage, so those were dropped; ' ... ' marks where a garbled Greek lemma, word or phrase was left out, and a sentence reduced mostly to such gaps was left out whole. Consecutive notes on one verse are combined into one entry, each written 'gloss) note' and joined with ' ... '; the heading is the gloss as printed where an entry holds a single lemma, otherwise ''. Short notes on neighbouring verses are combined into range entries; long notes (e.g. on 9:5) are cut at sentence ends into several entries. Editing otherwise limited to joining line ends and dropping running heads, page numbers and signatures, footnote markers, and all footnotes (the editor's ED./E. B./TR. notes and the V. g. footnotes from Bengel's German version); V. g. passages printed in brackets in the text are kept. The Bible text Logia uses has no Romans 16:25-27, so Bengel's notes on those verses are left out. Where the OCR lost a verse number the note stays with the verse before it (one, on 4:25, was placed by hand); no notes were found for 2:11, 2:23, 7:19, 12:4, 16:6 and 16:15, which Bengel either passes over or the OCR merged into a neighbouring note. English words the OCR garbled badly (e.g. 'adomed', 'pm*pose') may have been cut as Greek; English words misread in italic type ('ivhich', 'ice have') are fixed in library/corrections/bengel-romans.json only where certain, and other OCR slips are left (e.g. 'tenth' for 'with', stray '^' and '}' for brackets). The long outline of the epistle in the note on 1:16 is kept as printed.
